rationale: Clinical and genetic reports of patients with NAV3-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621182) consistently confirm intellectual disability and global developmental delay in 100% of reported individuals across all published cohorts. Severe expressive language delay or absent speech is universally documented across cohorts (e.g., Ghaffar et al., 2024; Kakar et al., 2025; Umair et al., 2024), and behavioral abnormalities (hyperactivity, autistic features, aggression, self-injury) as well as craniofacial dysmorphism are documented in the vast majority of cases (>75-100%). In addition, microcephaly, ocular anomalies, and skeletal features represent prominent recurring phenotypes across cohorts.

evidence.text: All eleven reported individuals from seven families harboring NAV3 variants exhibited intellectual disability, microcephaly, skeletal deformities, ocular anomalies, and behavioral issues, along with speech delay.

new_directions.question_text: What specific dysmorphic and ocular features reliably distinguish NAV3-related neurodevelopmental disorder from other tubulinopathy- and microtubule-associated syndromes?
new_directions.rationale: Microcephaly, ocular defects, and skeletal anomalies appear in 100% of the Ghaffar et al. cohort; delineating specific discriminating morphological signs will assist clinical differentiation before sequencing.

new_directions.question_text: Does variant class (biallelic loss-of-function vs. monoallelic de novo missense) modulate the penetrance and severity of seizures and microcephaly in NAV3 disorders?
new_directions.rationale: Truncating biallelic variants and dominant de novo variants have both been reported; defining genotype-phenotype correlations will improve prognostic accuracy.
